title: Original Japanese subtitle translation checks
notes: Original synthetic dialogue, not quotations from an anime. English references are for review and must never enter translation prompts. Adjacent cues provide context, not a single continuous story.

cases.japanese: 鍵をなくしたんじゃない。部屋に置いてきたんだ。
cases.reference: I didn't lose the key. I left it in my room.
cases.check: Preserve the correction: not lost, left in the room.

cases.japanese: じゃあ、取りに戻ろう。
cases.reference: Then let's go back and get it.
cases.check: Resolve the omitted object from the preceding cue.

cases.japanese: あと三分しかない。
cases.reference: We only have three minutes left.
cases.check: Preserve the scarcity implied by shika.

cases.japanese: まだ三分もあるよ。
cases.reference: We still have a whole three minutes.
cases.check: Preserve the contrasting reassuring emphasis.

cases.japanese: 彼が来るとは限らない。
cases.reference: He might not come.
cases.check: Uncertainty must not become certainty that he will not come.

cases.japanese: 来ないとは言ってない。
cases.reference: I didn't say he wouldn't come.
cases.check: Preserve the scope of negation.

cases.japanese: その箱、開けないで。
cases.reference: Don't open that box.
cases.check: Keep the prohibition.

cases.japanese: 開ける前に、先生に聞いて。
cases.reference: Ask the teacher before opening it.
cases.check: Preserve the order of actions.

cases.japanese: ミナは自分の弟を駅まで迎えに行った。
cases.reference: Mina went to the station to pick up her younger brother.
cases.check: Keep Mina as the person collecting the younger brother; gendered pronouns need not match the reference.

cases.japanese: 戻ってきたのは、弟だけだった。
cases.reference: Only the younger brother came back.
cases.check: Do not have both people return.

cases.japanese: 兄さんを待ってるんじゃない。姉さんを待ってるの。
cases.reference: I'm waiting for my older sister, not my older brother.
cases.check: Do not reverse the corrected family relationship.

cases.japanese: 明日は行けたら行く。
cases.reference: I'll go tomorrow if I can.
cases.check: Keep this conditional rather than a firm promise.

cases.japanese: 私が謝る筋合いはない。
cases.reference: I have no reason to apologize.
cases.check: Do not turn this idiom into an apology.

cases.japanese: 冗談に決まってるでしょ。
cases.reference: I'm obviously joking.
cases.check: Preserve the confident conversational tone.

cases.japanese: 別に、あなたのためじゃないから。
cases.reference: It's not as if I did it for you.
cases.check: Do not reverse the negative statement or invent a hidden confession.

cases.japanese: そんなこと、言うんじゃなかった。
cases.reference: I shouldn't have said that.
cases.check: Express regret about a past statement.

cases.japanese: もう少しで
cases.reference: I almost...
cases.check: Keep the fragment continued by the next cue.

cases.japanese: 約束を忘れるところだった。
cases.reference: ...forgot our promise.
cases.check: Almost forgot; do not claim the promise was actually forgotten.

cases.japanese: お待たせして、申し訳ありません。
cases.reference: I'm sorry to have kept you waiting.
cases.check: Keep the apology and polite tone.

cases.japanese: こちらこそ、急に呼び出してごめん。
cases.reference: I'm sorry for calling you here at such short notice.
cases.check: Preserve the responding apology rather than merely thanking the other speaker.

cases.japanese: 二人とも帰ったの？
cases.reference: Did both of them go home?
cases.check: Keep the question about two people.

cases.japanese: ううん。一人しか帰ってない。
cases.reference: No. Only one of them went home.
cases.check: Preserve the negative answer and the number one.

cases.japanese: 「行かないで」って言ったのに。
cases.reference: Even though I said, 'Don't go.'
cases.check: Preserve the quoted prohibition and unfinished contrast.

cases.japanese: 行ってしまった。
cases.reference: They went anyway.
cases.check: Past completed departure; gender is not specified.
